summary: This is a Makefile rule that finds all markdown files in the current directory and runs a shell script called concat.sh to process them. The 'concat' target depends on all .md files being present, so if any markdown files change, the rule will re-execute.

explanations.1: The colon creates a Make rule named 'concat'. The part after the colon (called 'prerequisites') lists what this rule depends on — here, it runs a shell command that finds all files ending in .md and feeds that list to Make as dependencies.
explanations.2: The tab character at the start is required by Make syntax; this is the actual command that runs when the rule executes, which calls the concat.sh shell script.
